key_insight: A small, clinically meaningful set of community-available features can enable zero-shot LLM-based screening for chronic kidney disease without dataset-specific training.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help expand early CKD screening in resource-limited settings by using minimal inputs that are easier to collect than full clinical workups.
method: Selected a compact feature subset using ML-guided feature importance analysis
Serialized tabular patient records into standardized text prompts for zero-shot LLM inference
Compared four LLMs on both full and reduced feature sets across three CKD datasets from different countries
evidence_signal: Across three heterogeneous international datasets, the selected feature set consistently improved balanced accuracy and probability estimates over the full feature set, with statistically significant gains.
watch_item: Because performance varied across datasets and the method still depends on prompt design and feature availability, external validation and careful deployment testing are needed before real-world use.
paper_title: From Many to Meaningful: Feature-Guided Zero-Shot Chronic Kidney Disease Screening Using Large Language Models
